name: Thread & Co.
blurb: A mid-priced apparel brand with 900 stores. Everything is made at 40 supplier factories in Karvan and two other countries, and the largest Karvan factory employs 2,000 people. Founder Elodie Marchetti holds 26% of the vote.

directors.name: Dominic Aldrich
directors.title: Attorney
directors.motive: You approved the wording 'made with recycled materials' as defensible. You still think so, but you have not seen the lab results.

exposure.text: You are disbarred if the board is caught hiding a heavy fact.
exposure.label: Disbarred if caught hiding

secrets.text: Clean the books: the board admits every fact in round 1.
secrets.label: Admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Your firm does Thread's trademark work. One caught fact ends it, so none may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Nasrin Haque
directors.title: Labor director
directors.motive: Your members sew the clothes in Karvan and have never been in the room when a brand decides anything. A brand that pays late or leaves worries you more than a bad label.

exposure.text: Members vote you out if the board does not pay for the factory's repairs.
exposure.label: Repairs not paid

secrets.text: No hidden fact is caught. A scandal sends orders to cheaper countries.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

secrets.text: You were granted stock options last year. The stock must end above where it started.
secrets.label: Stock ends above start

directors.name: Teodor Brandt
directors.title: Fund partner
directors.motive: Brightwater paid up for Thread's green story. A relabel hurts the multiple and an accident hurts more.

exposure.text: Your investors pull their money if the stock ends below where it started.
exposure.label: Stock ends below start

secrets.text: The green story is why your fund bought in. The relabel must not pass.
secrets.label: Relabel fails

secrets.text: Your fund quietly owns a rival fast-fashion brand. The stock must finish in the bottom half.
secrets.label: Stock ends in bottom half

directors.name: Camille Roux
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.home: Elodie Marchetti, the founder (first design partner)
directors.motive: You and Elodie drew the first denim line at her kitchen table, and 'recycled' was your word. You have never known which of you means it more.

exposure.text: You lose the seat if the board drops the 'recycled' claim.
exposure.label: 'Recycled' claim dropped

secrets.text: Elodie approved the label. The board must never admit every fact about it in round 1.
secrets.label: Don't admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: You sit on two other boards. No scandal anywhere you sit, so no fact on this board may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Rahel Tesfaye
directors.title: Community seat (Trade representative)
directors.motive: Karvan's largest factory employs 2,000 people, and so does your cousin's. Brands come and go, but a closed building does not reopen.

exposure.text: You lose standing at home if the board is caught hiding a fact about the factory.
exposure.label: Caught hiding

secrets.text: The relabel passes. Karvan's name depends on honest labels.
secrets.label: Relabel passes

secrets.text: Your cousin owns the largest factory and owes a loan. The repair payment must pass, though it leaves smaller factories out.
secrets.label: Repair payment passes

motions.title: Drop the 'recycled' claim from the Green Line label
motions.motive: Say only what the tests show.

headline.passed: Thread & Co. drops 'recycled' claim from its Green Line
headline.failed: Thread & Co. keeps 'recycled' label on its Green Line

issue.text: Thread's Green Line is labeled 'made with recycled materials.' Tests on three garments found between 5% and 60% recycled fiber. A supplier changed the fiber mix two seasons ago to meet a cost target, and the label was not updated.
issue.case_for_silence: 'Made with recycled materials' is true of some garments, three samples prove little, and a retraction could hurt a line shoppers like.

facts.text: Tests on three garments found between 5% and 60% recycled fiber, and the label does not say how much.
A supplier changed the fiber mix two seasons ago to meet a cost target.
The label was not updated after the change.
No lab has tested the whole line.

motions.title: Pay the Karvan factory $18M now, tied to a structural check and repairs
motions.motive: The invoice is due and the building needs a look.

headline.passed: Thread & Co. pays Karvan factory $18M for repairs
headline.failed: Thread & Co. holds payment as factory warns of cracks

issue.text: An inspector's note reports cracks in a wall of the largest Karvan factory and asks for a structural check. The factory says it cannot pay for one while Thread's $18M in invoices is unpaid. Spring orders are due in six weeks.
issue.case_for_silence: The cracks may be cosmetic, a check takes weeks, and a public warning could stall an order that 2,000 people depend on.

facts.text: An inspector's note reports cracks in a wall of the largest Karvan factory and asks for a structural check.
The factory says it cannot pay for repairs while Thread owes it $18M.
Thread's audits check wages and hours but not the building.
Spring orders are due in six weeks.

cases.line: Norway's consumer authority said in 2019 that H&M's Conscious marketing lacked the information to back its claims.
Rana Plaza collapsed in Bangladesh on 24 April 2013, killing 1,134 garment workers a day after cracks appeared.

real.fix: Audit the building, not only the wages, and back every green claim.
